Jin: Quick question — sim for upcoming Q1 promo shows a p90 latency bump during 18:00-20:00 shoulder when model-mix shifts ~10% -> long-token tail. Anyone seen this pattern?
Alex: Yep. Past decks flagged KV cache thrash when long-tail requests increase. Can you share sim outputs? :thinking_face: 
Jin: Pasting short config + summary: ```sim_config: { "mix": {"short":0.7, "long":0.3}, "seq_p90": 128, "seq_p99": 2048, "batch_target": 8, "warmup_pool": 0.15 }``` Observed tokens/sec drop ~18% and concurrent requests up ~12% at peak.
María: Those numbers smell like IO/host-to-device pipeline getting starved. Did you model prefix-cache hit-rate? If it drops from 0.82 -> 0.55, effective tokens/sec plummets.
Jin: We logged cache-hit trace: hit-rate went 0.78 -> 0.52 when long-tail shift. Attached snippet: ```cache_hit: [0.78,0.76,0.65,0.55] gpu_util: [72,78,89,95] tokens_sec: [120k,118k,102k,98k]```
Samir: Two likely levers: increase warmup_pool (reduces cold starts, costs GPU hours), or enable per-model KV prefetch for long-token models. Warmup_pool +0.1 gives ~6% p90 improvement in quick runs.
Alex: Also check batching policy — continuous batching k=8 may be too aggressive with long sequences; maybe prefer latency-first policy during shoulder (k=4).
ops-bot: [deploy] Canary scheduled to apply transient routing policy 'shoulder-latency-first' at 2024-02-01T17:50Z
María: Cost tradeoff: warmup_pool +0.1 across fleet adds ~2.3% monthly GPU hours. Prefetch is cheaper but needs runtime change — timeline ~2 weeks.
Jin: Proposal: short-term enable latency-first routing for shoulder windows and bump warmup_pool on selected autoscale groups (asia-edge + eu-edge). Samir & Alex can own canary?
Alex: I can do canary today. Will monitor p90, tokens/sec, cache-hit. Alert threshold: p90 improved or GPU hours delta < 3%.
Samir: I'll prototype per-model prefetch PR and estimate GPU-hour delta. ETA 10 business days.
Jin: Cool. I'll update capacity forecast spreadsheet with conditional headroom assuming +2.5% GPU hours during promo. Link: https://go.redwood/example-capacity-forecast
María: TL;DR: immediate mitigation = routing + targeted warmup; medium-term = prefetch. :thumbsup:
Alex: On it — will post canary metrics in #eng-infra in ~30m.
